1a5e95ea29520134aa86161df09979c2e217d020.summary: A 2017 blog post by Brian Reitz that builds a PowerShell proof of concept, using the PSReflect tool, to write a Windows registry Run key value whose name starts with a null character. The post links this persistence trick to Kovter malware. It says Regedit and similar tools fail to show the value, while the Sysinternals Autoruns tool still does. The author presents it to help defenders test detection of such registry persistence.

hedges: The author notes the value is not truly hidden: Regedit errors on it, but Autoruns still shows it and can delete it.
The author calls the null-character example relatively simple and gives an opinion on why studying such techniques matters.

1acc2a8d239c6e3174bbec8dcce33dc1175d6f02.summary: This page is a promotional landing page for a Qualys Threat Research Team report on Quasar RAT, an open-source remote access trojan. It invites readers to download the full report without registration. The page gives only a short overview and asks readers to download the rest, so it is treated as a marketing piece and the fact lists are left empty.
